title: Sgt. Verbeck’s “Barry White” Episode 😂 + NROs: The Blue Notebook Review
description:
This week’s Blue Notebook Review comes with a twist — Sgt. Verbeck is under the weather, but the show must go on… with an unexpected Barry White-style voice that you don’t want to miss.

While he powers through, our Neighborhood Resource Officers cover key highlights from providing updates on community engagement, enforcement activity, and the work happening across Santa Monica neighborhoods.

Stick around for the outtakes — they might be the best part.

As always, thank you for staying informed and engaged with SMPD.
transcript_text: Hello, Santa Monica and welcome to this week's Blue Notebook review. You may notice my voice is a little off and that's because I've been under the weather this week. But as they say in showbiz, the show must go on. So, I'll keep my part short and sweet. Let the NRO give you the meat and potatoes of this week's crime update. Unless you're vegetarian, then it's just the potatoes, maybe some tofu. Anyhow, let's get the ball rolling with Enopardo to talk to you about traffic. Izzy, it's all yours. >> Hey, Santa Monica. Let's get right into it. This week, we conducted 221 stops and issued 137 citations. So, yes, we were outside again. Now, the highlights. One driver decided to mix driving with drinking and struck a delivery driver. The driver was arrested for DUI. Another traffic stop turned into a Why do we have that moment? Officers recovered a loaded 9 millimeter with an extended magazine. The driver was arrested and distracted driving. We ran multiple operations and handed out citations like it was a rewards program. Except nobody wants those kinds of points. Bottom line, pay attention, drive smart, and let's all make it home without becoming the highlight next week. Unless you want to. See you later. Back to you in the studio, Sergeant Rick. >> Thanks, Izzy. and to address one of the comments by Ava Bird, who's one of our more zenful skeptics. I addressed how the money's allocated from each citation a few episodes ago. Feel free to rewatch it. And let's hear from Enro Hollowell to talk to you about crime. Thanks, Sergeant Rick. Officer Steven Hollowell here in the field, your B1 neighborhood resource officer. And for this operational period, Santa Monica police responded to 2573 calls for service as well as conducted 118 arrests. Good job, Santa Monica police. Way to work the beat. And for the two incidents of note, Santa Monica police responded to a pure fight which resulted in a shooting. Pier officers responded and located one victim. Santa Monica Police as well as Santa Monica Fire Department rendered immediate aid and transported that victim to the hospital. The Realtime Crime Center was able to track the suspect where they lost sight of him, but located him fairly quickly after at a local hospital and arrested that suspect after he was treated for his wounds. Santa Monica Police also conducted a multi- agency collaborative effort with the LA County Probation as well as our downtown service unit and our crime impact team which resulted in 13 arrests. Great job all around and back to you in the field or not in the field in the studio. Sergeant Rick, goodbye. >> Thanks Hol. You see, Carlos, the one we didn't forget to talk about the pier shooting. You just happened to be a week ahead of the update. And good job to the troops and and for the quick action on the Smart Center to get that suspect in custody so quickly. How about we go to NRO Tago to talk to you about our efforts in dealing with our homeless population. Officer Tago, what do you got? >> Hello, Santa Monica. Officer Tago here, your B3 neighborhood resource officer. Let's get straight into it. Here are your health team stats for the reporting period. Our health team responded to 242 radio calls, conducted 195 selfinitiated contacts, addressed 14 encampments, made 21 arrest, and issued 35 citations. And here's your incident of note. Officers contacted an individual who had recently become homeless after traveling from Texas for work. Through coordination with the Salvation Army, officers facilitated a Project Homecoming return, successfully reuniting the individual with family from Texas and removing them from homelessness locally. This is what the work looks like. Enforcement when needed, but also taking the time to connect people with real solutions and support systems. We're going to keep showing up, handling what needs to be handled, and making an impact where it counts. And from Tongville Park, back to you in the studio, Sarge. >> Thanks, Tago. And last but not least, let's hear from your B4 in a row, officer Aila, to talk about our community and youth engagement. Brandon, where where are you? >> You guys are doing great. Good job. Keep up the good work. >> Chef's got it. >> You got it. Hey folks, during this reporting period at the community engagement team, we continue to meet with neighborhood and business groups. We also held community events such as compression with a cop at Restore Hyper Wellness. Thank you, Michelle, for hosting that with us. We also conducted a community event at Douglas Park Wagwatch, which was a great turnout. Today, you can see the team. We're barbecuing for the PAL kids for their spring break. I'm going to keep it short this week, so that's all I have. Back to you in studio, Sarge. Thanks, Brandon. Tell Chef those burgers and hot dogs look amazing. And that, my friends, concludes this week's Blue Notebook review. And remember, be kind. It doesn't cost anything, but it can change everything.
